title: Zero-to-SampleApp: Lightweight Orbit Playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose and audience
This is a lightweight, opinionated playbook to get an engineer from zero to a simple SampleApp (codename: Orbit) that exercises the SDK, CLI runner, and a small telemetry surface so product and infra teams can iterate faster. Audience: new SDK adopters, solutions engineers, and internal demo builders.

Goals (what "success" looks like)
- Developer can run a local end-to-end demo in ~10 minutes (no infra account setup beyond an API key).
- Telemetry emits a minimal set of events visible in Redwood Console (latency, token usage, model selection).
- Quick checklist for typical failure modes and recovery path.
- Small sample config that can be reused by Solutions Eng for POC.

High-level flow
1) Clone sample-orbit-app repo (link in linked_artifacts).
2) Install dev CLI (npm/pip wrapper).
3) Create .env with REDWOOD_API_KEY and optional REDWOOD_ENVIRONMENT=staging.
4) Run local runner: ./orbit run --profile quickstart.
5) Open local UI (http://localhost:3000) and exercise the chat/generate flows.
6) Check Redwood Console for telemetry events under playbook/orbit-demo.

Quickstart (minimal commands)
# assumes node 18+, yarn installed
git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-orbit-app.git
cd sample-orbit-app
yarn install
cp .env.example .env # paste REDWOOD_API_KEY into .env
# start backend and frontend in one process for dev
yarn dev
# open http://localhost:3000 and click "Quickstart demo"

Opinionated config (example .env fragment)
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-live-XXXXXXX
REDWOOD_ENVIRONMENT=staging
ORBIT_PROFILE=quickstart
REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.staging.redwood.ai
TELEMETRY_TAGS=playbook:orbit,demo:true,team:devexp

Runner profiles (explaination)
- quickstart: small token limit (512) + greedy sampling to keep latency low.
- interactive: relaxed token limit (2048), streaming enabled, local caching on prefix.
- test-harness: deterministic sampling (seeded), captures full prompt+response for evals.

Sample runner config (YAML-style, included inline to avoid separate files)
profile: quickstart
model: redwood/gpt-1.3b
max_tokens: 512
temperature: 0.0
batch_window_ms: 30
enable_streaming: true
prefix_cache: enabled
telemetry: playbook/orbit-demo

Telemetry matrix (what we emit and why)
- orbit.runner.start (counter) -> track demos started per-team
- orbit.request.latency_ms (histogram) -> measure end-to-end latency for dev flows
- orbit.token.count (gauge) -> token usage per request; used for cost estimates in demo
- orbit.model.fallback (event) -> when runner falls back to smaller model, include reason label
- orbit.ui.error (counter + sample) -> capture user visible errors to guide UX fixes

Mapping to Redwood Console
- telemetry tag playbook:orbit will be auto-surfaced under a dashboard named "Playbook / Orbit". Add saved query: tag:playbook:orbit AND environment:staging.
- Suggested tracing hooks: attach request_id and local_session_id so traces can map to user flows.

Developer checklist (pre-demo)
- [ ] repo cloned and yarn install completes
- [ ] .env populated with a valid API key and base URL
- [ ] local port 3000 free (or change in .env)
- [ ] telemetry tags set to include team and demo name
- [ ] confirm redwood API is reachable (curl $REDWOOD_BASE_URL/health)

Common failure modes + recovery
1) 401 from Redwood API
   - symptom: UI shows "Auth error" and logs show 401
   - quick fix: ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is correct and not expired; test with curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" $REDWOOD_BASE_URL/v1/models
2) High latency > 3s for interactive flows
   - symptom: streaming stalls, UI spinner persists
   - quick fix: check runner profile batch_window_ms (lower to 0-10ms), disable streaming to test non-stream path, fall back to smaller model via config (model: redwood/gpt-0.6b)
3) Telemetry not appearing in Console
   - symptom: no events under playbook/orbit
   - quick fix: verify TELEMETRY_TAGS env; inspect runner logs for telemetry flush errors; confirm network egress to telemetry ingestion endpoint

Notes to self / FIXME (open questions)
- Should quickstart default to an ephemeral API key generated via "dev key" flow? (reduces support friction)
- Consider adding a tiny local LLM shim to let demos run completely offline for on-site events. Tradeoff: additional maintenance.
- Want to capture user prompt variations for a small sample set (privacy implications) — add opt-in checkbox in UI and document retention policy.

Testing matrix (manual + automated)
- Manual: basic path (open UI, send prompt, see response) on Mac/Win/Linux.
- Integration: CI job that runs runner in test-harness profile and asserts deterministic responses. Use GH Action: .github/workflows/orbit-ci.yml (PR in linked_artifacts).
- Perf smoke: script to pulse 10 parallel requests and assert p50 < 600ms for quickstart profile on staging.

Examples for solutions eng demos (two short scripts)
1) cost-demo.sh - runs a set of prompts and prints per-prompt token counts and estimated cost (uses token-count metric from telemetry).
2) fallback-demo.sh - intentionally saturates main model to trigger fallback; shows UI behavior and sends the fallback event for console demo.

UX script for a 10-min walkthrough
- 0:00 - intro + architecture diagram (5 slides)
- 2:00 - start the app (yarn dev) and explain runner profile
- 4:00 - demonstrate quickstart prompt and show Console telemetry appearing live
- 7:00 - trigger fallback-demo and discuss graceful degradation
- 9:00 - Q&A and next steps

Localization and multi-language notes
- Keep prompts and sample UI copy in a locale file (i18n/en.json) so Solutions Eng can swap strings for demos in EU/APAC.

Delivery artifacts to add before finalizing
- small diagram (PNG) for architecture: runner -> redwood api -> console
- one-pager with CLI commands only (for non-dev audience)
- privacy note template to include in demo slides

Links (quick copy)
- repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-orbit-app
- PR that added telemetry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-orbit-app/pull/42
- internal tracing doc: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OBS/Tracing+Hooks

Next steps (owners)
- Liam: wire up ephemeral dev-key flow (owner: Liam Chen) - target: 2026-02-20
- Sofia: add opt-in prompt capture UX and privacy blurb - target: 2026-02-14
- Marcus: add perf smoke GH Action and perf script - target: 2026-02-07

Last-minute notes
- Keep this playbook intentionally small; the goal is to reduce friction for the first demo. If it becomes too generic, split into two: (1) quickstart for devs, (2) solutions-eng field kit.

Scratchpad (short internal commands and tips)
- Enable verbose logs: export DEBUG=orbit:*
- Replay recorded session: node tools/replay.js --session sessions/2026-01-15-demo.json

-- end of draft --
